steps.title: The 10-second version
steps.text: Documents come in from customers, we read them with ML, a human checks the unsure ones, and the result is published to the customer's accounting software. Everything else supports that.

steps.title: 1 · Who uses it
steps.text: Customers send receipts from the web, mobile apps or by forwarding e-mail. Accountants work in the web app.

steps.title: 2 · The front door
steps.text: All traffic goes through the CDN and the API gateway. The gateway checks every request with the Auth service.

steps.title: 3 · Getting documents in
steps.text: Uploads and parsed e-mails are stored in the object store. An event goes on the ingest queue, so the user never waits for OCR.

steps.title: 4 · Reading the document
steps.text: A pipeline: OCR → classify → extract fields → check for duplicates. If the model isn't confident, the document goes to a person.

steps.title: 5 · The human in the loop
steps.text: Unsure documents go to the review queue. Ops fix them in the Review tool, and they rejoin the main path at the Documents API.

steps.title: 6 · The core
steps.text: The Documents API applies supplier rules, matches against bank transactions (via Plaid) and writes to the ledger.

steps.title: 7 · Getting it out
steps.text: Every change is an event on the bus. The Publisher sends it to Xero, QuickBooks or Sage, and other listeners handle notifications, analytics and audit.
